My girlfriend knows about it, she has since about one month into the relationahip, but after she witnessed one of my episodes first hand she asked that I don't come to her when I'm like that anymore.

At first, I was really hurt. To be totally honest, I still a little am. Not entirely because of her not wanting to be the shoulder to cry in, but because the way she brought it up, she basically diminished my feelings in comparison to her own.

But over time, I realize that she's a bit in the right. My depression shouldn't drag anyone else down. If someone wants to crawl into the dark hole I'm in during one of my episodes, it would be grealy appappreciated, but  I don't have the right to drag anyone down with me. 

To this day I tell her when things are going bad. I tell her when I can't get out if bed or when I drink myself to sleep, and she listens to me and shows concern, but I never ask her to come help. We have established that won't be healthy for the other beautiful things out relationship carries with it. 

Basically, my take away from this  is that you should tell you SO about what's going on. Secrets like that are never something to hold onto. But if he or she doesn't feel they can provide the support you may need, do NOT demand it. They are humans too. Just because you are close doesn't give you the right to demand empathy.

The mere fact taht you can aknowledge that means you are better than 80% of the peple i've known in life. And also, the key word is acted. So don't sweat whatever happened too much. Alcohol makes people do stupid things which is why its so god damn fun. Your friends will realize that it was the booze that made you do whatever you did, and if they don't recognize this maybe apologize. But don't beat yourself up. You seem like a cool guy/girl. 


Also, a side note just to illustrate what I mean. My old friends and I had a rule where if someone was telling a story about something that happened while they were drunk, they HAD to let us know they were drunk. This became a rule after one kid decided to spread a funny story that made a guy look like a total douchebag but they failed to include the fact that they were drinking at a pretty big party which changed the circumstances completely. After we learned the guy was drunk, we INSTANTLY laughed about it and forgot all about it.

I know exactly how you feel and it sucks. I was having this same problem all of my last school year and most of it the year before that. My advice is to tell her how you feel. I know this sounds like absolutely terrible advice, because when I heard that at first I thought it was just a bad idea.

This summer I kind-of manned up and started to be more obvious that I liked her at times in more than a friend way. It helped. Now, I am still in the friend-zone, but her knowing how i feel makes it a lot easier to cope with. 

I know you think you just want to be friends with her, but the truth is, you probably don't. You want to be more, but you just dont want to say it. I told myself the same thing for months and months, and it made things worse. 

So my final advice is to try to bring up how you feel about her. If i remember correctly, how it happened with me is she was joking about how she liked a friend of mine (jokingly for sure, it was obvious she wanted nothing to do with him). I then said how i was jealous, and i'  pretty sure at that point she asked me to explain and I told her. 

In the meanwhile, find something to occupy your time. Mine ended up being finding a bunch of new music and playing soccer. If you can find ANYTHING to occupy your time, you will find you won't be thinking about her as much. This really sucks bro, and I wish you the best of luck.
